en: The Therāpadāna: The Chapter on the Giver of Almsfood (Bhikkhadāyivagga) 5. The Apadāna of the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya [Verse 1] "O Blessed One, you who possess the ten powers, you who are the refuge for all beings, I offer this handful of flowers to you, the Teacher. [Verse 2] Having offered these five handfuls of flowers to the Buddha, the Great Sage, I was reborn in the world of the Thirty-Three, enjoying divine pleasures.

[Verse 3] For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the heavens; And for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a king, a lord of the earth. [Verse 4] In every birth I possessed great splendor and majesty; I was never born into a lowly family, nor did I suffer from poverty. [Verse 5] In whatever realm I was reborn, I was always honored by the people; By the power of that gift of flowers, I attained such glory. [Verse 6] In my final existence, I was born into a wealthy family; My parents were joyful, and they named me Muṭṭhipupphiya. [Verse 7] When I reached the age of sixteen, I went forth into homelessness; Having gone forth, I practiced the holy life under the dispensation of Kassapa. [Verse 8] I lived for twenty thousand years as a monk; I was diligent in my duties and devoted to the practice of meditation. [Verse 9] At the end of my life, I passed away from that human state; I was reborn in the Brahmā world, a realm of sublime radiance. [Verse 10] There I remained for sixty-four thousand aeons; Then, having fallen from there, I was reborn in the human world once more. [Verse 11] In this final birth, I have attained the supreme state; Through the merit of that offering, I have become an Arhat. [Verse 12] I am free from all defilements, cooled, and liberated; Today, I have realized the fruit of the path of non-returning. [Verse 13] I have seen the Buddha, the peerless one, the teacher of gods and men; I have heard his Dhamma, which leads to the cessation of suffering. [Verse 14] I have paid homage to the Teacher, the one with the ten powers; I have fulfilled my duty and attained the goal of peace. [Verse 15] This is the apadāna of the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya, Who, through the power of his offering, has reached the state of an Arhat. [Verse 16] May those who hear this apadāna, and those who recite it with devotion, All attain the supreme state, the cool and peaceful Nirvana. [Verse 17] By the power of this merit, may all beings be happy; May they cross over the ocean of saṃsāra and reach the further shore. [Verse 18] May the Buddhas protect us all, and the Dhamma and the Saṅgha; May we all attain the bliss of liberation, free from all suffering.

[Verse 19] Thus did the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya speak of his own past deeds; Having heard this, rejoice and strive to follow the path of virtue. [Verse 20] This is the apadāna of the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya, The fifth in the Chapter on the Giver of Almsfood. May it bring merit and happiness to all.
“Then, by the name Sudassana,
I was a garland-maker;
I saw the Buddha, free from passion.”
The eldest in the world, the bull among men—
taking a jasmine flower,
I worshipped Padumuttara.
With pure vision and a joyful mind,
I attained the divine eye through this offering of flowers.
And through the aspirations of my mind,
for a hundred thousand eons,
I did not fall into an evil rebirth.
Sixteen kings named Devuttara reigned thirty-six eons ago.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Muṭṭhipupphiya recited these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Muṭṭhipupphiya.
